sources.note: First-hand sketch + acoustic follow-up: six tones in open syllables (T1 33, T2 31, T3 453, T4 232, T5 34, T6 21, with proto-tone categories A1-C2) and two in checked syllables (45 <*D1, 21 <*D2); speakers under 25 realise T3 as high-rising [45] (Thai-like) and merge T4 [232] with T5 [34], so the 6-tone system becomes a 5-tone system in young speakers; attributed to contact with Standard/Northern Thai.

sources.note: Iu Mien has two complex contour tones, high rising-falling (T3) and low rising-falling (T4); replicating L-Thongkum (1988) 34 years later with 40 speakers aged 12-84 (isolation + carrier phrase, GAMM f0 modelling) confirms incremental change toward rising variants of T3 and T4; older speakers show peak delay only under short duration / preceding low tone, younger speakers generalise the rising contour; contact may have initiated the change but a phonetic peak-delay bias seeded it.
